conclusion.summary:
The meeting's answer is a calmer, more consistent version of the colours you already have, not a new look. All 25 specialists voted on every item. Their average score for the plan is 7.7 out of 10: 18 gave it 8 and 7 gave it 7.

The palette in words. The light grey page stays. White cards get a thin, light outline so groups don't melt into the page outdoors. There is one dark colour, the near-black green of the tab bar, and it means only two things: 'do this' (main buttons and every + button) and 'your numbers' (the calories and macros cards). Lime means only 'chosen, today, done, or how far you've got'. On a light background lime is almost invisible, so anything chosen also gets a dark edge and a tick. Deep green words always mean a link and are always underlined. The pale green Meal plan tint and the cream 'cook with what you have' tint stay, and each feature uses its tint on every card where it appears. Amber is kept for allergy warnings only, and red only for errors and for deleting things. No colour ever judges food, a price, a budget or going over a target: those are said in plain dark words.

What each kind of thing gets:
- Main buttons are dark with white words.
- Other buttons are white with a mid-grey outline (testers said grey buttons looked broken).
- A button you can't press yet is grey, with the reason written beside it.
- A choice shows an empty tick circle, and turns lime with a dark edge and a tick when chosen.
- Secondary text is a darker grey, because testers called it faint.
- Restaurant and shop logos sit on small white tiles, and their names are always written.

Your two requests:
- **Settings cog:** it now sits at the far top right of every page, not just the four tabs, as a white circle with the word 'Settings' under it.
- **Shopping list:** the Shopping list button sits just to its left on Home, Groceries and Eat out.
- Where something already sat in that corner, it moves: Save goes into the recipe sheet, and the restaurant star moves next to the restaurant's name.

The biggest changes from today:
- Dark 'selected' chips (Dinner, Thursday) become lime with a tick, so they stop looking like buttons.
- The three dark past days on Home become white, with a dot when you logged food, so today stands out.
- Grey pills (Back, Change, Select, Add, + and −) become white with an outline.
- Prices and big numbers that were green become dark.
- Lime comes off decoration: the icon circles, the More tile, the Scan card's button and 'Make a new plan'.
- Every allergy line, including the household's on the plan check, uses one amber note.
- The faint track on the numbers card gets brighter, so you can see where your target ends.
- The dial shows '1,580 left' in the middle instead of a percentage.

How the votes went:
- Agreed by nearly everyone: dark main buttons, the dark tab bar, the grey page, every + dark, retiring the separate protein/carbs/fat colours, and a dark Scan card button.
- Close calls:
  - The brighter dial track: 16 for, 8 wanted it fainter.
  - The outline on every button: most for, some worried about clutter.
  - Lime instead of dark for chosen things: most for, with a check that older testers find it just as clear.

What would raise the score:
- Your yes on the changes that undo your own earlier looks (they are in the questions).
- A before-and-after check with Frank, Harold, Irene, Raj and Joan on a real phone, outdoors and with the brightness turned down.
- A real-phone check that the brighter dial track doesn't look heavy.
- Building it once as shared pieces, with a test that blocks stray colours.

Nothing goes live until you say so. It stays on the iap branch, and the iPhone app gets it only in a build after 1.1 is reviewed.

palette.role: Page background behind every screen and the recipe sheet. Also the flat inset inside white cards: info tags, icon wells, the macro strip, step-number and rank circles, the segmented-control track, photo and pack-shot placeholders, loading skeletons, and the pressed state of white controls. Replaces #eef1ef, #f1f3f2 and #f3f6f4
Cards, sheets, Pip's speech bubbles, fields, secondary buttons, unselected chips and tiles, header controls, logo and pack-shot tiles

Solid 1px edge on cards, Pip's bubble (tail included) and logo/pack-shot tiles; row dividers; the empty part of progress bars on light surfaces (sun-deep is 3.67:1 against it); the fill of a button that can't be pressed yet (text-2 on it 6.13:1). Replaces rgba(17,24,20,0.08), #e9ecea and #e2e6e3

1.5px edge on every unfilled tappable control (secondary buttons, Back, cog, Shopping list pill, chips, fields, the stepper, segmented track), the 2px empty tick ring, radio ring, switch-off track and knob, the sheet handle, the dashed edge of the scan estimate, the water-bottle outline. 3.99:1 on white, 3.65 on page, 3.36 on the plan tint, 3.41 on the cook tint

Placeholder words in fields on white only (4.99:1). Also the empty part of the dial and bars on the ink numbers cards: 3.21:1 against ink, with lime 3.97:1 on it. This is the founder's white track made brighter, about 35% white over ink

Headings, body, every sentence a person must read, figures, prices, allergy-note words. 17.9:1 on white, 16.4 on page, 15.1 on the plan tint, 15.3 on the cook tint, 17.3 on note-bg. Text only, never a fill

One-line captions, units, counts, small labels, ticked-item names: 8.35:1 on white, 7.65 on page, 7.03 on the plan tint, 7.15 on the cook tint, 6.13 on line. Replaces #5f6361 (also inside the select-arrow SVG)

The one dark fill. Used for main buttons, every add (+), the tab bar, the day's numbers cards, toasts, the Contains box, the Premium badge, count badges, map pins, and the dark logo tile behind white-artwork logos. Replaces #0b1a12 used as a fill, #111, #0b0b0b and #09090b
Pressed and hover state of ink buttons, together with a 0.97 scale. 1.64:1 against ink, so the change is visible; white on it 9.75:1. Replaces #2c3530, which was only 1.26:1 from ink
Words, figures, icons and the toast's Undo on ink (16.0:1)
Labels on ink (Calories, Protein), unselected tab icons and words, paywall sub-lines, the Premium badge edge on ink surfaces (10.26:1). Replaces white/75 and white/40
Lime. Means chosen, today, where you are, done, or progress on ink. Never a button, banner, card fill, icon disc or decoration, and never on the plan or cook tint (1.06 and 1.07:1)
Words, ticks and dots on lime (11.86:1); the 2px edge around any lime item on a light surface (14.91 on white, 12.54 on the plan tint); today's ring on the week strip. Also Pip's own line colour

Progress on light surfaces: plan step bar, making-plan bar, ingredient match bar, the budget slider's best-fit band and dot (4.99:1 on white, 3.67 against the line track). Never text or icons, and never placed right next to accent. Replaces #8cc63f and #34d399

Underlined links, line icons in category tiles and tool rows (6.44:1 on white, 5.90 in page-fill wells), the 2px focus ring on light surfaces, the caret, iOS AccentColor and CSS accent-color. Never a figure, price, status line, error or button fill
Meal plan feature card only. Nothing lime and no bare Pip may sit on it
Every 'cook with what you have' card (Home, the Shopping list's 'What can I cook with this?', Recipes' 'Cook with what's on your list'). Nothing lime and no bare Pip may sit on it
Fill of the allergy note only
Full 2px border and triangle icon of the allergy note (4.84:1 on note-bg, 5.02 on white). Replaces #d97706 and #92400e. The note's words use text #0b1a12; #3b2a06 is retired

App errors and destructive actions only: words, circle-! icon, 4px banner bar, 2px wrong-field edge, the 1.5px edge on destructive buttons, the confirm button's fill (white on it 6.57:1). Never on food, figures, prices or targets
Behind an app error banner (danger words 6.05:1 on it, text 16.5:1)

Controls and pills floating on photos (Back, cog, expand, heart, kcal pill), with a soft shadow. Tappable ones also get a 1px #7a817d edge, the kcal pill a 1px #d9dedb edge. Ink on it is 15:1 or more over any photo
Behind sheets and dialogs. Neutral black so food photos don't turn olive. Replaces rgba(11,26,18,0.55), bg-black/60-65 and the 0.28-0.62 overlays
The light dimming behind Pip's tips (older testers were flustered by heavy dimming); the lit control is ringed in ink
Only over a full-bleed photo hero, so the iPhone status bar stays readable. The only overlay allowed on a food photo

rules: Ink #1d2320 means 'do this' or 'your numbers'. It is the only dark fill: main buttons, every add (+), the tab bar, the day's numbers cards, toasts, the Contains box, small badges, map pins and dark logo tiles. #0b1a12 is for text only.
At most one full-width ink button is in view at a time. Repeated adds are compact ink pills, and alternatives (other shops) are secondary.
A main button sitting on an ink surface is white with ink words.

Lime #d6efa0 means chosen, today, where you are, done, or progress on ink. It is never an action (including toast Undo), a banner, a card fill, an icon disc, a badge fill, a tick bullet or decoration, and never on either feature tint.
On a light surface every lime item has a 2px #052e16 edge and a mandatory mark: a tick for choices, a dot for radios, days and 'where you are' chips. Its words are #052e16 and bold.
An unchosen choice shows an empty 1.5px #7a817d tick ring in the tick slot, so a choice never looks like a button and the words never jump when ticked.
Every unfilled tappable control is white with a 1.5px #7a817d edge. Tappable cards and rows keep the 1px #d9dedb line and show an ink chevron or a photo.

A #d9dedb fill means only 'can't press yet'. It is pill-shaped, with the reason in #0b1a12 above it. Never fade a control with opacity, and never grey out a Premium-locked control: it keeps its working colours, a lock and the badge.

Things you can't tap never look like buttons: 6px corners, no edge, no chevron. This covers info tags, the Premium badge and the Contains box. On the page, a tag is white with the 1px line; inside a card it uses page fill.

Words on light surfaces are #0b1a12, or #4a4f4c for one-line captions only. Placeholders are #6b716e and only on white. On ink, words are white or #c9d1cc. Any sentence a person must read is #0b1a12. Small labels are sentence case, semibold, at least 13px; no spaced capitals.

Green words (#046c4f) are always an underlined link, in short runs. Status lines ('Added', 'You have 1 of 3') are #0b1a12 with an icon, or a toast. A price that opens a shop's site is #0b1a12, underlined, with an external-link icon.
Progress on ink is lime on #6b716e. Progress on a light surface is #4d7c0f on #d9dedb. The figure is always written beside it. #4d7c0f never sits right next to accent.
Never colour food, a figure, a price, a budget, a rank or going over a target by meaning. Going over is said in words in the same colour ('120 kcal over', '18 g over', '£4 over your budget').
There is no reward colour, glow or confetti for eating or for streaks. A day's dot means only 'logged'. Compare has no winner colour, and ranks have no medal colours.
Pip's face never reacts to what or how much was eaten, or to a budget.
Protein, carbs and fat are told apart by their words and fixed order, never by hue.

Amber (#fffbeb fill, full 2px #b45309 border, triangle icon, a heading word, #0b1a12 words) is only for the person's or household's own allergens, Contains matches and 'not checked for your diet', with at most one per screen view. Generic 'check the label' lines are info tags.

Red #b42318 is only for app errors (a 4px left bar, circle-! icon and title on #fef3f2, or a 2px field edge with icon and message) and for destructive actions. Neither amber nor red ever touches a food figure or a price.
Each feature keeps one tint everywhere it appears: Meal plan #e4f0d0, every 'cook with what you have' card #fbeccb, Scan your food white. Words on tints are #0b1a12 or #4a4f4c.

The same thing looks the same on every screen. The header order is Back or title, then the page action, then the Shopping list pill, then the cog with the word 'Settings' far right, on every page except Settings itself, sheets and full-screen camera. Back always shows the word. The Premium badge, toast, stepper, chips, numbers card and allergy note are each one component.

A chain's or shop's colour exists only inside its unmodified logo file, on a white tile with a 1px #d9dedb line (an ink tile for white artwork), with padding proportional to the tile and the radius on the tile, never clipping the file. The name is always written beside it. Loyalty-scheme colours are never borrowed.
Food photos get no overlay, tint, filter or text, except the neutral top status band on hero photos. Only photo chips sit on them. A chosen photo card is marked on its frame.
Pip and the app icon are fixed brand art (allow-listed). Pip sits on no disc, never on lime, a tint, the numbers cards, a safety note or next to a logo, and may sit on ink.

The stroke scale has five widths: 1px structural lines; 1.5px every control edge, destructive included; 2px chosen edges, tick and radio rings, today's ring, the allergy note border and a wrong field; 3px focus and coach rings; 4px banner left bars.
Edges are real CSS borders, so they survive forced-colours mode, with 2px of space reserved so states never shift the layout. Ticks are SVGs drawn in currentColor.

Contrast: text at least 4.5:1 (aim 7:1); control edges, ticks, chosen edges and progress at least 3:1 against what is next to them. Check every new pair on page, card, line and both tints, and on ink.

Every colour comes from a token in globals.css. No raw hex, Tailwind palette colour or bg-[#…] in app components outside the allow-list (Pip, app icon, water, FSA lights, Apple/Google buttons, the map 'you' dot). A test enforces this.
Shadows are faint on cards and stronger only on floating layers (sheets, toasts, sticky bars, photo chips).
